M02.intro: My work is where you act on everything waiting for you: decisions on requests, workflow tasks, reminders, your own requests and notifications. As organisation administrator you also use it to keep requests moving and to raise requests for others.
M02.why: Undecided requests hold up leave, attendance, expenses and payroll inputs. Knowing how the inbox, send back, reassignment and delegation work lets you unblock a request without going around its approvers.
M02.who: Everyone has My work and Notifications. The Inbox opens with task.view or task.view_all, or any approval right. Managers approve their team's leave and attendance (leave.approve, attendance.approve). HR Manager and Tenant HR Admin hold task.* (reassign, mark not relevant). Auditor sees all tasks read-only. Tenant Super Admin holds every key.
M02.where: My work › Overview, Inbox, Task inbox, Team HR requests, My requests, New request and Notifications. The inbox actions (send back, bulk approval, discussion, delegate, archive) are switched on in Admin › Setup › Automation.
objectives: Decide requests from the Inbox: approve, reject, send back and approve several at once where it is switched on.
Find a stuck request and unblock it: reassign the task, or hand approvals to a colleague while someone is away.
Raise and follow requests for yourself or on someone's behalf, and keep your notifications under control.

procedures.title: Decide a request from the Inbox
procedures.before: You hold the approval right for the request type and the employee is within your access scope. You cannot decide your own request.
steps: Go to My work › Inbox. The heading shows how many items are new, for example "Inbox · 8 new".
Click a type on the left, for example Leave 4, or search. Use Filters for employee, dates or leave type.
Click the item. The panel shows the reason, who else is away, the balance before → after and the employee.
Click Workflow and policy to see who has decided so far, who it waits with and the policy behind it.
Click Approve, add an optional note and confirm. The next item opens.
Click Reject, type the reason the requester will see, and confirm.
procedures.result: The module applies the decision (for leave, the balance changes), the requester is notified and the audit trail records who decided and why.

procedures.title: Switch on the inbox actions your organisation wants
procedures.before: settings.update (Tenant Super Admin, Tenant HR Admin, Account Owner). Agree with HR which request types should allow each action.
steps: Go to Admin › Setup and choose Automation.
Move to the Inbox actions step. Each action lists the request types it is switched on for.
Choose types for Bulk approval, Discussion, Send back, Delegate and Move to archive. An empty list keeps the action off.
Switch on bulk archiving, choose manual or every night, after how many days, and the types never archived.
On the Review step give the Reason for change and click Save settings.
procedures.result: Approvers see the new actions on items of those types in the Inbox, Approval Center and Task inbox. Out of office appears in the menu once a type is delegable.

procedures.title: Send a request back for changes, and resubmit it
procedures.before: Send back is switched on for the request type. It is offered for workflow steps, leave, time office requests, loans, reimbursement claims and profile changes.
steps: In the Inbox open the request and choose Send back.
Type what the requester should change (required) and confirm. The item leaves the approvers' queues.
The requester opens My work › Task inbox › Sent back to me and sees your note under What to change.
They click Resubmit, add an answer if needed, and confirm.
The request returns to the same approval step with a fresh round of approvers.
procedures.result: The request is corrected without being rejected and raised again. The run log and audit trail keep both the send-back and the resubmission.

procedures.title: Approve several requests at once
procedures.before: Bulk approval is switched on for the request type in Admin › Setup › Automation.
steps: In the Inbox choose the request type, for example Leave.
Tick the items to approve. Only types switched on for bulk approval can be ticked.
Optionally type a Note for the approvals; it is added to each one.
Click Approve selected. Each item is checked and recorded on its own, up to 100 at a time.
A message gives how many were approved and lists any not approved with the reason.
procedures.result: The selected requests are approved one by one; a refusal on one (for example balance) does not stop the others. Rejections stay one at a time, with a reason.

procedures.title: Unblock a stuck workflow step by reassigning it
procedures.before: task.view_all and task.reassign (Tenant Super Admin, Tenant HR Admin, HR Manager). Find out why it is stuck: the approver left, is away or lacks rights.
steps: Go to My work › Task inbox › All open tasks. Overdue due dates are red.
Click Open run to see the run log and who the task is assigned to.
Back in the list click Reassign. Choose A person or Everyone holding a role.
Pick the person or role and give the Reason. Nobody can receive a request they started or that is about them.
The new assignee is notified and sees the task under Waiting for me.
procedures.result: The step continues with the new approver; the run log and audit trail show the move, from whom, to whom and why.

procedures.title: Hand your approvals to a colleague while you are away (out of office)
procedures.before: Delegate is switched on for at least one request type in Admin › Setup › Automation. You hold task.delegate (task.delegate_any to do it for someone else).
steps: In the menu open Workflows › Out of office. It appears only once delegation is switched on.
Choose the colleague, the first and last day (not in the past, at most 366 days) and the request types.
Type the reason (up to 500 characters) and save. The colleague is notified.
The colleague sees your items in their Inbox and Task inbox, marked as on your behalf, and decides with your authority.
On your return, end the period from the same page with a reason.
procedures.result: Requests keep moving while you are away. The audit shows the colleague deciding on your behalf. Nobody decides their own request, and delegations do not chain.

procedures.title: Raise a request on an employee's behalf
procedures.before: You hold the module's on-behalf right (for example leave.manage for leave, attendance.manage for regularisation).
steps: Go to My work › New request.
Search, or scroll to Raise for someone, and click the type, for example Leave.
The module's form asks whom the request is for. Pick the employee.
Complete the form. The employee's own policy decides what is allowed.
The request follows its usual approvals; find it in the Inbox of its approvers or the module's list.
procedures.result: A request raised for the employee, under the module's rules for requests made on someone's behalf.

procedures.title: Clear and organise your notifications
procedures.before: None.
steps: Click the bell or go to My work › Notifications.
Click Needs attention or Approvals first; tick Unread only to hide what you have seen.
Click Open on a notification to go to the record it is about.
Snooze one For an hour, Until tomorrow 9:00 or For a week if it is not for now.
Click Mark all read when you have seen the rest.
procedures.result: Only what still needs you stays unread; snoozed items come back on their own.

warnings.title: Who decides a request
warnings.headline: A request is decided either directly by holders of the approval right, or by its workflow when one runs on it.
warnings.body: With no workflow, leave goes to people with leave.approve whose access scope reaches the employee (normally the manager). With a published workflow, the workflow's approvers decide it.
points: Nobody decides their own request or one about themselves.
A Manager with no access scope reaches every employee, so they could approve anyone's leave.
As Tenant Super Admin you can approve almost everything; leave decisions to the right approvers.
warnings.todo: Give managers an access scope (M05) before relying on direct approvals.

warnings.title: Inbox actions are off until you switch them on
warnings.headline: Send back, Bulk approval, Discussion, Delegate and Move to archive are all off by default.
warnings.body: Until a request type is listed for an action, approvers only Approve or Reject it, and the card says the request can't be sent back.
points: Settings are in Admin › Setup › Automation, step Inbox actions.
Expense reports and compensation changes keep their own return action.
Archiving only hides an item from one person; reminders and escalation still run.
warnings.todo: Decide per request type with HR and switch on only what you need.

warnings.title: Task inbox is not the whole inbox
warnings.headline: The Task inbox lists only workflow steps and onboarding tasks.
warnings.body: Leave, attendance, expense and other requests decided without a workflow appear in the Inbox and the Approval Center, not in the Task inbox.
points: Use the Inbox to see every decision.
Use Task inbox › All open tasks to find and reassign stuck workflow steps.

warnings.title: Reassigning and delegating keep the rules
warnings.headline: You cannot use reassignment or delegation to let someone approve their own request.
warnings.body: A task is never reassigned to the person who started the request or the person it is about. A delegate never decides their own request, and delegations do not chain.
points: Reassign needs task.reassign and a reason.
A delegate decides with the delegator's authority, and the audit says so.

troubleshooting: An approver says the request is not in their inbox
They lack the approval right, the employee is outside their access scope, or a workflow now decides it.
Check their roles and scope (M05); open Workflow and policy on the request to see who it waits with.
work/inbox
A manager sees requests from the whole organisation
The manager's user has no access scope, so it reaches every employee.
Edit the user and add an access scope (for example their team) in Admin › Setup › Users.
work/my-work
There is no Send back button
Send back is not switched on for that request type, or the run was started by the system.
Switch it on in Admin › Setup › Automation › Inbox actions, or reject with a reason.
work/inbox
Out of office is not in the menu
No request type is switched on for Delegate.
Add request types under Delegate in Admin › Setup › Automation › Inbox actions.
work/task-inbox
A workflow step waits for someone who has left
The task is assigned to that person or to a role nobody active holds.
Task inbox › All open tasks › Reassign; set a role reliever or the manager reliever for the future.
work/task-inbox
The decision fails with "This item is no longer waiting for your decision"
Someone else decided it, it was withdrawn, or your rights changed.
Refresh the inbox; check the request's trail with Workflow and policy.
work/inbox
Opening a notification does nothing
You may not open the record it is about, or it no longer exists.
Read the notification text; ask someone with access to the record.
work/notifications
An employee cannot raise a request type
No policy gives it to them, they lack the right, or the employee request lock is on.
Check their policies (M06) and roles; New request shows a lock notice when a lock applies.

M05.intro: This module is where you decide who can sign in to PeopleOS, what each person may do (roles and permissions) and whose data they may reach (access scope and data access groups). It also covers the security policy, single sign-on and the integration area: API keys, webhooks, the integration hub and the reference data that other systems rely on.
M05.why: Access that is too wide exposes salaries, bank details and personal data; access that is too narrow stops approvals and payroll. Every grant you make is audited, so mistakes are traceable but not undone automatically.
M05.who: Tenant Super Admin holds every permission and is the only role that can give Tenant Super Admin. Account Owner can invite users, give roles and set the security policy. Tenant HR Admin manages users, integrations and security but can only view roles. Auditor can view users and roles.
M05.where: Admin › Setup › Users, Roles and Data access groups; Admin › Platform › Security policy, Single sign-on, API keys, API reference, Integration hub, Inbound events, Webhooks, Webhook deliveries, Log exports, JV codes, Exchange rates, Country packs, Data export and Product ideas.
objectives: Invite a user, link them to their employee record, give roles and set their access scope following least privilege.
Explain how roles, access scope and data access groups combine, and remove access correctly when someone leaves.
Set the security policy and manage single sign-on, API keys, webhooks and integrations safely.
depends_on: M03 Organisation structure: companies, locations, departments, grades and other units are the values you choose in an access scope
M07 Employees: an employee record is linked to a sign-in (Login user, or Sign-in › Invite to sign in)
M06 Workflows and policies: workflow steps route approvals to roles, so role holders and relievers decide who approves
M04 Masters and configuration: if configuration approval is on, edits to roles, single sign-on and webhooks wait in the Change Centre
M09 Exit and alumni: the HR clearance step Roles held and Complete exit remove a leaver's access
M23 Audit: every role, scope and security change is recorded in Change history

fields.label: Departments
fields.meaning: Limit to employees in these departments.

fields.label: Business units
fields.meaning: Limit to employees in these business units.

fields.label: Establishments (statutory data)
fields.meaning: Limit statutory data to these registered establishments.

fields.label: Divisions
fields.meaning: Limit to employees in these divisions.

fields.label: Teams
fields.meaning: Limit to employees in these teams.

fields.label: Designations
fields.meaning: Limit to employees with these designations.

fields.label: Grades
fields.meaning: Limit to employees in these grades.

fields.label: Levels
fields.meaning: Limit to employees at these levels.

admin/users--create.after: The user is saved with status Invited and e-mailed a temporary password that works for a limited time. At the first sign-in they choose their own password and become Active. The role grant is recorded as Role Changed in the audit trail.
admin/users--create.permission: user.create to create; user.assign_roles to set Roles and Access scope (without it those steps are read-only).
admin/users--create.depends: Companies, locations, departments and other units must exist before you can choose them (M03).
admin/users--create.limits: This form does not link the user to an employee. Link them on the employee's Edit profile (Login user) or invite from the employee profile instead.

admin/users--edit.purpose: Changes a person's account, status, roles and access scope, and offers the Account menu for invitations, temporary passwords, reset links, MFA reset and signing out everywhere.
admin/users--edit.when: When someone changes role, moves to another company or location, is suspended or returns, or is locked out.
elements: Account, Roles, Access scope, Review: open any step; changes are listed for review before you save.
Header menu: new invitation or temporary password, revoke invitation, reset link, MFA reset, Sign out everywhere.
Active or Suspended. Suspended stops sign-in at once. Invited is shown locked until the person accepts.
Roles given by hand; roles held through a membership rule are listed below and change only with the rule.
The person's organisation limits, plus the data access groups they belong to.
Table of every audited change: When, Action, By, Changes, Reason and Effective date.
Shown for other users only (never yourself). Removes the sign-in permanently. Prefer Suspended.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: The person's full name.

fields.label: Email address
fields.meaning: Changing it re-invites an invited user, or asks an active user to verify the new address.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Active lets the person sign in; Suspended blocks sign-in. Locked while Invited.

fields.label: Country
fields.meaning: Narrows the time-zone list; not saved.

fields.label: Time zone
fields.meaning: The person's time zone.

fields.label: Roles
fields.meaning: Roles given by hand. Removing is always allowed; adding follows the giving rules.

fields.label: Companies … Levels (Access scope)
fields.meaning: Same ten dimensions as on New user. Values in one dimension are OR; dimensions are AND.

fields.label: Reason for change
fields.meaning: Why you made the change; kept in the audit trail.

admin/users--edit.after: Saving applies at once: role changes are audited as Role Changed with what was granted and removed, and the person's permissions are refreshed. Suspended people cannot sign in.
admin/users--edit.permission: user.update to edit and use the Account menu; user.assign_roles for roles and scope; security.manage also for Generate a temporary password and Reset multi-factor authentication; user.delete to delete.
admin/users--edit.limits: You cannot reset your own MFA or sign yourself out everywhere here. If the employee's status is listed under Disable login, a daily check suspends the sign-in again.

admin/roles.purpose: Lists the roles of your organisation: the 16 system roles PeopleOS provides and any custom roles you add, with their status, reliever, number of permissions and number of users.
admin/roles.when: When you check what a role allows, create a custom role, or review who holds powerful roles.
elements: Opens Roles by person: each user with all their roles, read-only.
Creates a custom role from the permission catalogue.
Ticked for roles PeopleOS provides. System roles cannot be deleted or made inactive.
The person who takes the role's new workflow approvals while nobody active holds it.
How many permissions the role grants and how many users hold it.
How many self-service pages are hidden from this role's holders.
Show active or inactive roles. An inactive role grants nothing.
admin/roles.permission: role.view to see; role.create, role.update, role.delete to manage. Tenant HR Admin and Account Owner have role.view only.
admin/roles.limits: In the example organisation 16 roles are listed; Tenant Super Admin holds 309 permissions, HR Manager 107 and Performance Admin only 3 (view company, organisation and people setup).

admin/roles--create.purpose: Creates a custom role: its name, identifier, status and reliever, the permissions it grants, and the self-service pages its holders should not find in My space.
admin/roles--create.when: When no system role fits a job, for example a read-only payroll reviewer or a regional HR role.
elements: Name, slug, description, status and reliever.
Tick permission keys (area.action) from the catalogue; search and select all are available.
Tick self-service pages to hide from holders. It hides only; it never grants.
Check the role before creating it.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: The role's display name. Typing it fills the slug.

fields.label: Slug
fields.meaning: Stable identifier used by policies and integrations. Letters, numbers, dashes.

fields.label: Description
fields.meaning: What the role is for, so reviewers understand it.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Active or Inactive. Inactive grants no permissions and gets no new workflow tasks.

fields.label: Reliever
fields.meaning: Active user who takes the role's new workflow approvals while nobody active holds it.

fields.label: Permissions
fields.meaning: What holders may do. You can add only permissions you hold yourself.

fields.label: Leave out of My space
fields.meaning: Self-service pages hidden from holders' My space, favourites and search.

admin/roles--create.after: The role is created and its permissions are recorded in the audit trail as Role Changed. Nobody holds it until you add members or give it on a user.
admin/roles--create.limits: Permission keys come from the PeopleOS catalogue; you cannot invent new keys.

admin/roles--edit.purpose: Changes a role in four steps (Role, Permissions, Pages in My space, Review) and manages who holds it: by hand (Members), by rule (Membership rules), with the full History.
admin/roles--edit.when: When a job's responsibilities change, when you add or remove holders, or when you set a reliever for approvals.
elements: Role, Permissions, Pages in My space, Review: open any step, then review your changes before saving.
Tick or untick keys. Adding is limited to keys you hold; removing is always allowed.
Who holds the role, their employee code, companies, how it was given and status. Add member / Remove.
Pick a user, optionally Limited to company, and give a reason. Audited.
Rules that give the role automatically to people who match conditions, while they match.
Three steps: Rule, Who (Every or Any condition matches), Review with how many people match today.
Every audited change to the role.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: Display name of the role.

fields.label: Slug
fields.meaning: Identifier. Locked for system roles.

fields.label: Description
fields.meaning: What the role is for.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Locked for system roles: they stay active; remove members instead.

fields.label: Reliever
fields.meaning: Takes the role's new workflow approvals while nobody active holds it.

fields.label: Permissions
fields.meaning: What holders may do.

fields.label: Leave out of My space
fields.meaning: Self-service pages hidden from holders.

fields.label: Reason for change
fields.meaning: Why the role changed.

admin/roles--edit.after: Changes apply to every holder at once and are audited as Role Changed with the keys granted and removed. If configuration approval is on, the edit waits in the Change Centre and the role stays unchanged until approved.
admin/roles--edit.permission: role.update to edit; user.assign_roles and user.view for Members and Membership rules.
admin/roles--edit.limits: No membership rule may give Tenant Super Admin or Account Owner; give those by hand. Editing a system role changes it for everyone who holds it.

admin/data-access-groups.purpose: Lists data access groups. A group narrows what its members see inside one module (for example Payroll) to certain employees, on top of each member's own access scope.
admin/data-access-groups.when: When a person must see everyone in one area but only some people in another, for example all employees in Workforce but only one company in Payroll.
elements: Creates a group in four steps.
The area the group narrows: Workforce (people everywhere), Time office, Payroll, Performance, Engage, Expense or Asset.
By organisation unit, or Specific employees.
How many users are in the group and how many unit or employee values it reaches.
OK, or a warning that the group is not valid and its members see nobody until it is fixed.
Removes the group with a reason; members get back what their own scope allows.
admin/data-access-groups.permission: Changing groups needs user.assign_roles (and a reason for every change).
admin/data-access-groups.depends: Users and organisation units must exist.
admin/data-access-groups.limits: The example organisation has no data access groups yet.

admin/data-access-groups--create.purpose: Creates a data access group: its module, the people it reaches (by unit or named employees, optionally with reportees), and its members.
admin/data-access-groups--create.when: When a module needs narrower data access than the person's general access scope.
elements: Basis, unit values or employees, sub-departments and reportees.
Check and give the reason for change (required).

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: A clear name, for example Payroll – Demo Services only.

fields.label: Module
fields.meaning: Workforce narrows people data everywhere; another module narrows only that module's records.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Active or Inactive. Inactive groups do nothing.

fields.label: Description
fields.meaning: Why the group exists.

fields.label: Basis
fields.meaning: By organisation unit, or Specific employees.

fields.label: Companies … Levels
fields.meaning: Unit values the group reaches. Dimensions are AND; values within one are OR. None = whole organisation.

fields.label: Departments include the departments below them
fields.meaning: A department value also reaches its sub-departments.

fields.label: Employees
fields.meaning: Named employees (with basis Specific employees).

fields.label: Members also see
fields.meaning: Nobody beyond the rules, Their direct reports, or Everyone below them (all levels).

fields.label: Users in this group
fields.meaning: Who the group narrows. Members always still see themselves.

fields.label: Reason for change
fields.meaning: Why you created or changed the group; required.

admin/data-access-groups--create.after: The group applies immediately to its members in that module. Each member sees only the people the group reaches (plus themselves), and never more than their own access scope allows.
admin/data-access-groups--create.limits: A group can only narrow access, never widen it. Several active groups of the same module add up. A malformed group shows a warning and its members see nobody.

admin/security-policy.purpose: Sets your organisation's sign-in and retention rules in six steps: Access, Passwords, Disable login, Retention, Data warehouse feed and Review. Saved from Review with Save policy.
admin/security-policy.when: At go-live, after a security review, or when your IT policy changes (for example making MFA mandatory).
elements: IP allowlist, required authenticator-app MFA, and sign-out after idle minutes.
Minimum length, expiry, reminder, reuse limit and strict-password options.
Employee statuses in which sign-in is turned off automatically.
Days to keep AI interactions, notification deliveries, report runs and API call logs. Audit events are never purged.
Opt-in daily export of non-sensitive datasets and how long snapshots are kept.
Check all values and save. Each setting change is recorded.

fields.label: IP allowlist
fields.meaning: Exact IPs, 10.0.* wildcards or CIDR blocks. Empty = no restriction.

fields.label: Require authenticator-app MFA for every tenant login
fields.meaning: Everyone must use an authenticator app code at sign-in.

fields.label: Sign out after idle minutes
fields.meaning: Signs out inactive sessions. 0 = never.

fields.label: Minimum length
fields.meaning: 8 to 64 characters; 10 by default.

fields.label: Expire after days
fields.meaning: 0 = never. An expired password is changed at the next sign-in; SSO sessions are not affected.

fields.label: Remind before expiry (days)
fields.meaning: Reminder by in-app message and e-mail; 0 = none. 7 by default.

fields.label: Recently used passwords that cannot be reused
fields.meaning: 0 = no restriction; up to 24.

fields.label: Strict password: also require a symbol
fields.meaning: Adds a symbol to the standard rule (upper and lower case, a number).

fields.label: Strict password: refuse the person’s name, e-mail or employee code
fields.meaning: Blocks personal details inside passwords.

fields.label: Employees in these statuses cannot sign in
fields.meaning: For example Notice Period, Exited, Suspended. Sign-in returns when they leave the status.

fields.label: AI interactions / Notification deliveries / Report runs & exports / API call logs
fields.meaning: Days each kind of record is kept (365, 180, 90, 90 by default).

fields.label: Export datasets to the warehouse disk every day
fields.meaning: Off by default. Non-sensitive fields only.

fields.label: Keep daily snapshots for (days)
fields.meaning: 0 = keep.

admin/security-policy.after: Rules apply from the next sign-in or request. Turning on MFA makes each person set up an authenticator at their next sign-in.
admin/security-policy.limits: Working statuses (Joined, Probation, Confirmed, Active) cannot be chosen under Disable login, so one setting can never lock out the whole workforce. Where the warehouse feed is delivered is set up by PeopleOS; ask PeopleOS support before turning it on.

admin/single-sign-on.purpose: Lists single sign-on connections so people sign in with your identity provider (Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta or another OpenID Connect provider) instead of a PeopleOS password.
admin/single-sign-on.when: When your organisation wants staff to use their company account to sign in.
elements: Adds a connection to your identity provider.
Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta or Generic OpenID Connect.
The address that starts SSO sign-in (/sso/{slug}/redirect). Copyable.
E-mail domains allowed to use the connection; Any when empty.
Whether a sign-in is created on first login for someone without one.
When the connection was last used; Active or Disabled.
admin/single-sign-on.depends: An application registered at your identity provider (client ID and secret).
admin/single-sign-on.limits: The example organisation has no SSO connection. Only OpenID Connect providers are offered.

admin/single-sign-on--create.purpose: Creates an SSO connection: provider endpoints and credentials, allowed domains, whether new users are created on first login and which role they get.
admin/single-sign-on--create.when: When you connect PeopleOS to your identity provider.
elements: Name, slug, provider (fills the endpoints from a preset), client ID and secret, scopes and endpoints.
Allowed domains, auto-provisioning, role for new users, primary login and status.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: Name of the connection, for example Company Microsoft login.

fields.label: Slug
fields.meaning: Part of the login URL /sso/{slug}/redirect.

fields.label: Provider
fields.meaning: Choosing one fills the endpoints and scopes from a preset.

fields.label: Client id
fields.meaning: From the application registered at your identity provider.

fields.label: Client secret
fields.meaning: From your identity provider. Stored hidden.

fields.label: Scopes
fields.meaning: Normally openid profile email.

fields.label: Authorization endpoint
fields.meaning: Replace {tenant} or {domain} placeholders from the preset.

fields.label: Token endpoint
fields.meaning: Provider's token address.

fields.label: Userinfo endpoint
fields.meaning: Provider's user profile address.

fields.label: Allowed domains
fields.meaning: E-mail domains that may use this connection. Empty = any domain.

fields.label: Create users on first login
fields.meaning: On: a sign-in is created for a new person. Off: only existing users can use SSO.

fields.label: Role for new users
fields.meaning: Given to every user the connection creates. Never Tenant Super Admin; must be a role you may give.

fields.label: Show SSO as the primary login for this tenant
fields.meaning: Presents SSO first on the sign-in page.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Active or Disabled.

admin/single-sign-on--create.after: The connection is saved. A person signing in through it is matched to an existing user by e-mail; if none exists and auto-provisioning is on, a new active user is created with the chosen role.
admin/single-sign-on--create.depends: Client ID and secret from your identity provider.
admin/single-sign-on--create.limits: Users created by SSO are not linked to an employee record; link them on the employee's Edit profile (Login user). Edits are high-risk configuration: with configuration approval on they wait in the Change Centre.

admin/api-keys.purpose: Issues and manages API keys that let other systems (recruitment, attendance devices, finance) call the PeopleOS API. Each key has scopes, optional IP and rate limits, and a call log.
admin/api-keys.when: When you connect another system to PeopleOS, rotate a key, or investigate API use.
elements: Creates a key with a name, description, expiry, scopes, allowed IP addresses and requests per minute. The secret is shown once.
Opens the list of API endpoints and the scope each needs.
What the key may do, for example employees.read or attendance.write.
Any, or how many addresses are allowed.
Last used at / Expires at / Status
When the key was last used, when it stops working, and whether it is active.
Details shows API calls, Security events and 30-day usage. Regenerate replaces the secret at once; Revoke stops the key.
admin/api-keys.permission: api_key.view to see keys, logs and the API reference; api_key.manage to issue, edit, regenerate and revoke.
admin/api-keys.limits: The example organisation has no API keys. PeopleOS keeps only a hash: a lost secret cannot be shown again; regenerate the key. Without Requests per minute the API-wide limit applies (shown as a hint).

admin/api-reference.purpose: Shows every endpoint of the PeopleOS integration API with its method, path, purpose, required scope and parameters, and lets you download the description as OpenAPI JSON for your developers.
admin/api-reference.when: When you plan an integration and must decide which scopes a key needs.
elements: Endpoints grouped by area: Assets, Attendance, Employees, Leave, Payroll, SCIM, Workflows and more.
The call your developer makes and its purpose.
The API key scope the call needs. Give keys only the scopes they use.
A file your developers can load into their tools.
admin/api-reference.limits: Maintained by PeopleOS: it is generated from the live API, so it always matches what PeopleOS offers. In the example it lists 132 endpoints.

admin/integration-hub.purpose: Registers the external systems your organisation exchanges data with. Each has a code used in its inbound address, a signing secret, accepted event types, external references and value mappings.
admin/integration-hub.when: When another system will post events to PeopleOS (for example background verification results) or keep its own ids for PeopleOS records.
elements: Registers a system; its signing secret is shown once.
Code appears in the inbound URL /api/v1/integrations/{code}/events; Kind is the type, e.g. Recruitment / ATS.
Whether events must carry a valid signature.
When the signing secret was last changed.
Issues a new secret at once; the old one stops working.
Inbound events, External references (retire one) and Mappings (Add mapping).
admin/integration-hub.permission: integration.view to see; integration.manage to register, rotate, map, retire and reprocess.
admin/integration-hub.depends: An API key with the integrations.write scope for the system to post with.
admin/integration-hub.limits: The example organisation has no integration systems. Systems and references are retired, never deleted.

admin/integration-hub--create.purpose: Registers a new external system and its inbound security: whether events must be signed, the timestamp window, which API key may post and which event types are accepted.
admin/integration-hub--create.when: Before another system starts sending events to PeopleOS.
elements: Signature, timestamp window, bound API key, accepted event types.
Check before creating. The signing secret is then shown once: copy it.

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short code used in the inbound URL. Cannot be changed later.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: The system's name.

fields.label: Kind
fields.meaning: Type of system. Cannot be changed later.

fields.label: Require signed events (HMAC-SHA256 over "timestamp.body")
fields.meaning: On by default. Unsigned events are refused.

fields.label: Timestamp window (seconds)
fields.meaning: How old a signed event may be: 30 to 900, 300 by default.

fields.label: Only this API key may post (optional)
fields.meaning: Bind the system to one key; otherwise any key with integrations.write.

fields.label: Accepted event types (empty = every registered handler)
fields.meaning: For example reference.link, reference.retire, bgv.results.

admin/integration-hub--create.after: The system is registered and a signing secret is shown once in a notice. Give it to the other system's team through a secure channel.
admin/integration-hub--create.depends: An API key with the integrations.write scope.
admin/integration-hub--create.limits: PeopleOS accepts only the event types it has handlers for (reference.link, reference.retire and bgv.results).

admin/inbound-events.purpose: Shows every event other systems have posted to PeopleOS, with its integration, type, status, attempts and error. Payload contents are never displayed, only their keys, size and checksum.
admin/inbound-events.when: When an integration reports that data did not arrive, or to check that events are being processed.
elements: When, from which system and what kind of event.
The sender's id for the event.
Received, Processing, Succeeded, Retrying, Failed (refused) or Dead letter.
How often PeopleOS tried, and the last error.
Idempotency key, correlation id, payload keys, size and SHA-256, result and last error.
For failed or dead-letter events: queue it again with a reason.
admin/inbound-events.permission: integration.view to see; integration.manage to reprocess.
admin/inbound-events.limits: Event payloads are deleted after a short period set by PeopleOS; the event record stays. Events cannot be created or edited by hand.

admin/webhooks.purpose: Lists webhook endpoints: addresses in your other systems that PeopleOS calls when chosen events happen (for example employee.joined or payroll.finalized), with their success rate and failures.
admin/webhooks.when: When another system must react to PeopleOS events, or when deliveries start failing.
elements: Adds an address and the events to send to it.
Opens Webhook deliveries for every endpoint.
Delivered ÷ attempted. Green from 95%, amber from 80%, red below.
Count of failed deliveries for this endpoint.
Posts a sample event marked test, built from placeholder values.
New secret at once; the old one also signs for a grace period of 1 to 72 hours.
admin/webhooks.limits: The example organisation has no webhooks. PeopleOS tries a delivery up to 5 times before marking it Dead letter.

admin/webhooks--create.purpose: Creates a webhook endpoint: its name, HTTPS address, signing secret, status and the events PeopleOS sends to it.
admin/webhooks--create.when: When a receiving system is ready and you know which events it needs.
elements: Name, Url, Secret, Status and Events on one step.
Generated for you; the receiver uses it to check the X-PeopleOS-Signature header.
Tick the events to send, or Select all.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: Name of the receiving system.

fields.label: Url
fields.meaning: HTTPS address of the receiver. Unsafe internal addresses are refused.

fields.label: Secret
fields.meaning: Signing secret, pre-filled with a random value. Copy it for the receiver.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Active sends events; Paused sends nothing.

fields.label: Events
fields.meaning: Which PeopleOS events are sent, for example leave.approved or exit.completed.

admin/webhooks--create.after: From now on each chosen event creates a delivery to this address, signed with the secret. Watch them under Webhook deliveries.
admin/webhooks--create.depends: A receiving system that accepts HTTPS POST requests.
admin/webhooks--create.limits: Webhook edits are high-risk configuration: with configuration approval on they wait in the Change Centre.

admin/webhook-deliveries.purpose: Every delivery of every webhook endpoint with status, attempts, HTTP answer and latency. You can replay or acknowledge failures and export the log.
admin/webhook-deliveries.when: When a receiving system misses events, or as a routine check of failed deliveries.
elements: All deliveries, Failed deliveries (not yet acknowledged) and Waiting to retry.
Queues a CSV of deliveries for chosen dates and filters (no payloads); collect it in Log exports.
Pending, Delivered or Dead letter; tries; receiver's answer; response time.
Details, Retry now (pending), Replay (failed) and Acknowledge (with an optional note).
Webhook, Event, Status, Acknowledged, From and Until.
admin/webhook-deliveries.limits: Deliveries are created by PeopleOS only; you cannot add one by hand.

admin/log-exports.purpose: Lists the log exports you asked for (webhook deliveries or API calls) with their filters, status and row count, and lets you download the ready CSV.
admin/log-exports.when: After you request Export CSV on Webhook deliveries or on an API key's API calls tab.
elements: Queued, Running, Ready or Failed, and how many rows.
Downloads the CSV. Only you can download your own exports. Audited.
admin/log-exports.permission: The permission of the log: webhook.manage for deliveries, api_key.view or api_key.manage for API calls.
admin/log-exports.depends: An export requested from Webhook deliveries or an API key.
admin/log-exports.limits: You see only your own exports. Files are deleted after the Report runs & exports retention period in the Security policy.

admin/jv-codes.purpose: Keeps the accounting (journal voucher) code of records such as companies, departments, branches, employees and pay components, used when PeopleOS builds the payroll journal for your books.
admin/jv-codes.when: Before you export the first payroll journal, and when your chart of accounts changes.
elements: Choose a dimension, the PeopleOS code of the record, optionally an accounting system, and the JV code.
Company, Branch, Sub branch, Business unit, Department, Sub department, Designation, Employee, Grade, Level, Region, Pay component and more.
The PeopleOS record and its ledger or segment code.
Every system, or one system whose own code wins for it.
admin/jv-codes.permission: integration.view to see; integration.manage to set, change and remove.
admin/jv-codes.depends: The records (M03) and pay components (M12) must exist with codes.
admin/jv-codes.limits: The example organisation has no JV codes yet. Without a JV code the payroll journal uses the PeopleOS code. Several records may share one code.

admin/exchange-rates.purpose: Keeps exchange rates into and out of your base currency, by effective date. PeopleOS uses the latest rate on or before a date, for example for foreign-currency expenses and salaries.
admin/exchange-rates.when: When you pay or reimburse in another currency, typically monthly.
elements: Shown under the title. In the example organisation it is INR.
One rate: From, To, Rate and Effective on.
One effective date, many currencies into the base currency.
1 unit of From = Rate units of To.
From when the rate applies, and how it was entered.
admin/exchange-rates.limits: The example organisation has no rates. A rate saved for the same currency and date is replaced. Without any rate on or before a date, conversion is refused.

admin/country-packs.purpose: Shows the country packs PeopleOS provides (India, UAE, UK, US, Singapore, Australia, Canada): currency, time zone, financial year, tax and social security frameworks, labour defaults and which of your companies use each.
admin/country-packs.when: When you set up a company in a new country, or to check which rules apply to a company.
elements: Country name and code, currency, locale, time zone, financial year start, and full or generic statutory engine.
For example Income-tax Act 1961 and EPF, ESI, PT, LWF, Gratuity for India.
Standard weekly hours, notice days, minimum leave, overtime multiplier.
Your companies using the pack, by the company's country.
admin/country-packs.limits: Maintained by PeopleOS; you can view it only. India uses the full statutory engine; packs marked generic do not have the same statutory calculations, so ask PeopleOS support before paying people there.

admin/data-export.purpose: Requests a complete, encrypted export of your organisation's data. PeopleOS prepares it in the background; you download it here and open it with a passphrase shown to you.
admin/data-export.when: For your own archive, an audit, or when moving data to another system.
elements: Asks for a new package; you must say why.
Requested, Status, Records / files and Available until.
A link that works for a few minutes and only for you. Audited.
Shows the passphrase that opens the package. Showing it is recorded.
admin/data-export.permission: data.export (Tenant Super Admin and Account Owner).
admin/data-export.limits: Only one export is prepared at a time. A package is available for a limited time, then deleted. Credentials and secrets are never included. Keep the passphrase apart from the file.

admin/product-ideas.purpose: Sends your organisation's improvement ideas to Markedge's product team (the PeopleOS provider) and shows each idea's status and Markedge's response.
admin/product-ideas.when: When your team finds something PeopleOS should do better.
elements: Wizard: What it is about, The challenge, The ideal solution, Impact and files, Review.
The idea, the area it concerns and whether it is a new feature or an improvement.
Submitted, Under review, Planned, In progress, Released or Declined.
The product team's answer. The sender is told when the status changes.
admin/product-ideas.limits: Ideas are answered by PeopleOS, not by your organisation. Do not put employees' personal data in the text or files (PDF, JPG, PNG only).

procedures.title: Give an employee a sign-in from their profile
procedures.before: The employee exists with a valid work e-mail that no other user has, and is not exited or suspended.
steps: Go to People › Lifecycle › Employees and open the person's profile.
Click Sign-in › Invite to sign in. It is greyed out with the reason if the person cannot be invited.
Confirm with Send invitation. A sign-in is created from the work e-mail, linked to the employee, with the Employee role if you may give it.
Click Sign-in › Roles and access to open the user and add, for example, Manager.
On Admin › Setup › Users the person shows status Invited until they choose their password.
procedures.result: A linked sign-in. The person receives a temporary password by e-mail and becomes Active at the first sign-in.

procedures.title: Invite many employees at once
procedures.before: Employees have work e-mails. You hold user.create (and user.assign_roles to choose roles).
steps: Admin › Setup › Users › Invite to sign in.
What to send: Send to new user. Choose Roles for the new sign-ins (Employee is pre-filled) and, if wanted, Copy (CC) a notice to.
Pick employees by filters or codes. Sign-in filter defaults to No sign-in yet and Invited, not accepted yet.
See who will be sent what; anyone who cannot be invited is listed with the reason. Click Start.
procedures.result: Each eligible employee gets a linked sign-in and an invitation e-mail; the run keeps a delivery list.

procedures.title: Create a user who is not an employee yet, then link them
procedures.before: Decide the roles and access scope the person needs.
steps: Enter Name and Email address; check Country and Time zone.
Choose only the roles the job needs.
Choose companies, locations or other units to limit whose data they reach, or leave empty for the whole organisation.
Review and create. The user is Invited and e-mailed a temporary password.
When the employee record exists, open it, Edit profile, and choose this user in Login user.
procedures.result: An invited user with the right roles and scope, linked to their employee record when one exists.

procedures.title: Help someone who cannot sign in
procedures.before: Find the user under Admin › Setup › Users and note the Status.
steps: Open the user › Account › Send a new invitation. The earlier invitation stops working.
Account › Send password reset link. The person chooses a new password; you never see it.
Account › Generate a temporary password (needs security.manage). It is shown once to hand over.
Account › Reset multi-factor authentication with a reason. They set up a new authenticator at next sign-in.
Set Status to Active with a Reason for change. If their employee status is listed under Disable login, change that first.
procedures.result: The person can sign in again, and every step is in the user's History.

procedures.title: Create a least-privilege custom role
procedures.before: Write down the tasks the job needs. You can add only permissions you hold yourself.
steps: Enter Name (the Slug fills itself), Description, Status Active and, if useful, a Reliever.
Search and tick only the keys needed, for example payroll.view without payroll.finalize.
Optionally hide self-service pages that do not apply to these holders.
Review and create. The permissions are audited as Role Changed.
Open the role › Members › Add member, choose the user, optionally Limited to company, give a reason.
procedures.result: A role that grants exactly what the job needs, held by the right people.

procedures.title: Give a role automatically with a membership rule
procedures.before: The role is not Tenant Super Admin or Account Owner, and you hold every permission it grants.
steps: Admin › Setup › Roles › Edit the role › Membership rules › Add rule.
Choose Every condition matches or Any condition matches, then add conditions such as department or designation.
See how many people match today and give the Reason for change.
procedures.result: Everyone who matches (employed, with a sign-in that can be used) holds the role while they match; grants by hand are not affected.

procedures.title: Limit a payroll user to one company in Payroll only
procedures.before: The user holds Payroll Admin and has no access scope (sees everyone).
steps: Admin › Setup › Data access groups › New data access group.
Name it, choose Module Payroll and Status Active.
Basis By organisation unit; Companies: the one company; Members also see: Nobody beyond the rules.
Give the reason and create. Check that the Check column shows OK.
procedures.result: In payroll records the user sees only that company's employees (and themselves); other modules are unchanged.

procedures.title: Make MFA mandatory and tighten passwords
procedures.before: Tell staff they will need an authenticator app on their phone.
steps: Turn on Require authenticator-app MFA for every tenant login; set Sign out after idle minutes, for example 30.
Set Minimum length, Expire after days and Remind before expiry (days); turn on the strict-password options if wanted.
Choose statuses such as Notice Period and Exited in which sign-in is turned off.
Go through Retention and Data warehouse feed, then Review › Save policy.
procedures.result: Everyone sets up an authenticator at their next sign-in and passwords follow the new rules.

procedures.title: Issue an API key for another system
procedures.before: Know which endpoints the system calls (see API reference) and, ideally, the IP addresses it calls from.
steps: Admin › Platform › API reference: note the Scope of each endpoint the system needs.
Admin › Platform › API keys › Issue key. Enter Name, Description and an Expires at date.
Tick only the scopes noted. Avoid sensitive scopes unless required.
Enter Allowed IP addresses and, if needed, Requests per minute.
The key is shown once in a notice. Copy it and pass it to the system owner securely.
procedures.result: An active key limited to the scopes, addresses and period the integration needs, with every call logged.

procedures.title: Fix failed webhook deliveries
procedures.before: The receiving system's owner has fixed the cause (address, certificate or outage).
steps: Admin › Platform › Webhook deliveries › Failed deliveries tab; use Error breakdown to see causes.
Details shows the delivery history, payload and last response.
On Webhooks, use Send test on the endpoint to confirm it answers.
Tick the failed deliveries and use Replay selected, or Replay on one row.
For failures that need no resend, Acknowledge with a note so they leave the failure count.
procedures.result: Missed events reach the receiver again and the Failed deliveries tab is clear.

procedures.title: Request a full export of your data
procedures.before: You hold data.export.
steps: Admin › Platform › Data export › Request a full export; enter Why do you need it?
The export is prepared in the background and appears in the Exports table when ready.
Click Download; the link works for a few minutes and only for you.
Click Show passphrase and store it separately from the file.
procedures.result: An encrypted package of your organisation's data and the passphrase to open it, both recorded in the audit trail.

calculations.title: Webhook success rate (30 days)
calculations.intro: The Webhooks list shows, for each endpoint, the share of deliveries created in the last 30 days that were delivered, out of those attempted. Illustrative numbers: the example organisation has no webhooks.
explain: Delivered ÷ attempted × 100, rounded down. No attempts shows —.
95% and above green, 80–94% amber, below 80% red: 94% shows amber.
Admin › Platform › Webhooks, column Success rate (30 days).

calculations.title: Using an exchange rate in the other direction
calculations.intro: If only one direction is entered, PeopleOS works out the reverse as 1 ÷ rate, rounded to 8 decimals, using the latest rate on or before the date. Illustrative numbers.
explain: Direct rate if one exists for that date, else 1 ÷ the reverse rate, 8 decimals.
The latest rate with Effective on on or before the transaction date.

calculations.title: When a password expires and when the reminder comes
calculations.intro: With Expire after days set, a password expires that many days after it was last changed. The person is reminded once, in-app and by e-mail, inside the reminder window. Illustrative dates.
explain: Expiry = last change + Expire after days. Reminder window starts Remind before expiry days earlier.
The person must choose a new password at the next sign-in. SSO sessions are not affected.

warnings.title: How permissions work: module, page and action
warnings.headline: Each permission is one key, area.action, for example payroll.view, payroll.approve or payroll.finalize.
warnings.body: A role is a set of keys. A person's rights are the keys of all their active roles together. Inactive roles grant nothing.
points: Module and page: a menu or page appears when one of your active roles holds the key it needs.
Action: viewing, creating, approving and finalising are separate keys, so you can allow one without the other.
Sensitive data: employee.sensitive.view shows bank and statutory details, and each view is audited.
Company: a role given through Members can be Limited to company.
Pages in My space only hides self-service pages; it never grants anything.
warnings.todo: Read a key's description in the Permissions step before ticking it.

warnings.title: Roles for administrators
warnings.headline: Five roles carry organisation-wide or oversight rights.
warnings.body: These roles come with PeopleOS. Their names and permissions can be edited, but they cannot be deleted.
points: Tenant Super Admin: every permission; the only role that can give Tenant Super Admin.
Account Owner: companies, organisation, employees, users and role grants, settings, security, data export. No payroll or sensitive data.
Tenant HR Admin: configures almost every HR module, users, integrations, SSO, webhooks and security; can view roles only.
Auditor: read-only across modules with full audit access, including chain verification.
Executive: Workforce Command Centre and dashboards; no transactional access.
warnings.todo: Give these roles to as few people as possible.

warnings.title: Roles for specialists
warnings.headline: Specialist roles cover one area of HR operations.
warnings.body: Give the one that matches the job, then limit its data with an access scope.
points: HR Manager: employees, positions and lifecycle, leave, onboarding, exit, letters, service desk, workflows and reports.
HR Executive: day-to-day HR: add and update employees, tasks, onboarding, documents; views users.
Payroll Admin: all payroll, bank and statutory details, compliance reports, expense payment, audit view.
Attendance Admin: attendance set-up and exceptions; views leave and policies.
Expense Admin: expense set-up, policies, decisions and payments; exchange rates.
Asset Admin: company assets and related tasks.
Performance Admin: as delivered only views company, organisation and people setup; add performance keys if needed.
warnings.todo: Check each specialist role's Permissions step once before go-live.

warnings.title: Roles for managers, employees and outsiders
warnings.headline: Most people need only self-service, plus Manager if they lead a team.
warnings.body: Employee is the default role for invited employees.
points: Manager: approves the team's attendance, leave and expenses; team performance, learning and exit clearance.
Employee: own profile, leave, regularisation, payslips, claims, requests and tasks.
Alumni: a former employee's alumni portal and own payslips.
External user: a business partner without an employee record; their own tasks only.
warnings.todo: Give Manager together with an access scope so the manager does not reach the whole organisation.

warnings.title: Least privilege
warnings.headline: Give each person only what their job needs, for only the people they work with.
warnings.body: Start from Employee, add one role for the job, then narrow whose data with access scope and data access groups.
points: Prefer a custom role over adding keys to a system role.
Keep Tenant Super Admin to two trusted people so one can cover the other.
For holidays, hand approvals over with Out of office or a role Reliever, not with extra roles.
Remove roles when someone changes job; review access every quarter.
warnings.todo: Run the quarterly access review checklist at the end of this module.

warnings.title: Your settings and what PeopleOS maintains
warnings.headline: Most of this area is yours to set; a few parts are provided and maintained by PeopleOS.
warnings.body: Your organisation sets and is responsible for everything it can edit here. Parts maintained by PeopleOS you can view only.
points: Yours: users, roles, access scope, data access groups, security policy, SSO, API keys, webhooks, integrations, JV codes, rates.
Maintained by PeopleOS: country packs, the API reference, the permission catalogue and the API-wide rate limit.
Also set by PeopleOS: webhook retry attempts (5), how long inbound payloads and export packages are kept, the warehouse feed location.
Some features are switched on per organisation by PeopleOS, for example bulk employee import and export.
Product ideas are answered by Markedge's product team.
warnings.todo: Ask PeopleOS support about anything marked maintained by PeopleOS.

warnings.title: Empty access scope means the whole organisation
warnings.headline: A user with no access scope reaches every employee for the permissions their roles give.
warnings.body: Roles decide what someone may do; access scope decides whose data. The Manager and HR roles include employee.view, so without a scope those users can open every employee's record.
points: Dimensions combine with AND: Company X and Location Y means people in both.
Values inside one dimension combine with OR.
People always see themselves and their current reportees.
warnings.todo: Set an access scope for every user who should not see the whole organisation, especially managers and regional HR.

warnings.title: Who may give which role
warnings.headline: Only a Tenant Super Admin can give the Tenant Super Admin role.
warnings.body: Below Tenant Super Admin you may give a custom role only if you hold all its permissions, and any system role except Tenant Super Admin. So an Account Owner can give Payroll Admin.
points: You can add to a role only permissions you hold yourself.
Membership rules never give Tenant Super Admin or Account Owner.
SSO can never give Tenant Super Admin to new users.
Removing roles is never restricted.
warnings.todo: Keep Tenant Super Admin to two trusted people and give everyone else narrower roles.

warnings.title: Editing a system role changes it for everyone
warnings.headline: System roles can be re-permissioned, and the change applies at once to every holder.
warnings.body: System roles cannot be deleted or made inactive, but their permissions can be edited. A removed key is lost for all holders; an added key is gained by all.
points: The Performance Admin role as delivered only views company, organisation and people setup; add performance keys or use a custom role.
The Auditor role includes webhook.manage, which also allows changing webhooks.
warnings.todo: Prefer a custom role for a special case; record a Reason for change for every edit.

warnings.title: Suspend instead of delete
warnings.headline: Delete removes the sign-in for good and unlinks it from the employee.
warnings.body: Setting Status to Suspended stops sign-in at once and keeps the account, its roles and history for review. Completing an exit already suspends the leaver's sign-in.
points: You cannot delete yourself.
Use Sign out everywhere to end open sessions immediately.
warnings.todo: Use Suspended for leavers and long absences; delete only accounts created by mistake.

warnings.title: Secrets are shown once
warnings.headline: API keys, integration signing secrets and rotated webhook secrets are displayed a single time.
warnings.body: PeopleOS keeps only a protected copy. If the secret is lost you must regenerate or rotate it, and the system using the old one stops working.
points: Regenerate stops the current API key at once.
Rotate secret on a webhook keeps the old secret signing for 1 to 72 hours.
warnings.todo: Copy each secret straight into the receiving system or a password manager; never e-mail it.

warnings.title: Changes may wait for approval
warnings.headline: If configuration approval is on, edits to roles, SSO connections and webhooks are not applied at once.
warnings.body: They are parked in the Configuration Change Centre as high-risk changes and the record stays unchanged until someone approves.
points: You see the notice Submitted for approval with a change number.
warnings.todo: Check Admin › Setup › Change Centre after such an edit.

troubleshooting: User says the invitation does not work
The temporary password has expired, or a newer invitation replaced it.
Open the user › Account › Send a new invitation.
admin/users--edit
User cannot sign in, status Suspended
Suspended by hand, by completing their exit, or by the Disable login rule for their employee status.
If they should work, set Status to Active with a reason; check Security policy › Disable login.

User cannot sign in from the office or home
Their address is not in the Security policy IP allowlist.
Add the address or range under Access › IP allowlist, or ask them to use an allowed network.

The domain is not in Allowed domains.
Add the domain on the connection.
admin/single-sign-on--create

None of their active roles holds the permission the page needs, the role is inactive, or the grant is limited to another company.

A self-service page is missing from My space
One of the person's roles leaves it out, and no other role keeps it in.
Untick it under Pages in My space on the role.

Open Data access groups; fix the group whose Check column shows a warning, or switch it off.

The role is Tenant Super Admin, or a custom role with permissions you do not hold.
Ask a Tenant Super Admin to give it.

An integration's calls are refused

Open the key's Details › API calls to see the HTTP status; adjust scopes, IPs or regenerate.
admin/api-keys
checklist: Run the User access review report
Insights › Analytics › Report library: User access review, Active users without two-factor, Dormant users.
Review Tenant Super Admin holders
Filter Users by Roles = Tenant Super Admin; keep only those who truly need it.
Review powerful roles
Check holders of Payroll Admin, Tenant HR Admin, Account Owner and Auditor on each role's Members tab.
Suspend leavers and dormant accounts
Users with Last login at Never or long ago, and anyone who has left.
Check access scopes
Managers and regional HR should have a scope; empty means the whole organisation.
Check data access groups
Every group shows OK in Check; members are still right.
Review role changes
Look for Role Changed events in Change history for the quarter (M23).
Review membership rules
On each role, check rules and the number of Holders by this rule.
Review API keys
Revoke unused keys; check Last used at, expiry, scopes and IP limits.
Review SSO and webhooks
Disable unused connections and pause unused endpoints; clear failed deliveries.
Confirm the security policy
MFA, idle sign-out, password rules and Disable login statuses still match your IT policy.
summary: Roles decide what a person can do; access scope decides whose data; data access groups narrow one module further.
Empty access scope means the whole organisation. Scope dimensions combine with AND, values within one with OR.
Only a Tenant Super Admin gives Tenant Super Admin; others give only roles within their own permissions or system roles.
Administrators never see passwords: use invitations, reset links or a temporary password shown once.
Suspend rather than delete; completing an exit suspends the sign-in and Roles held hands over the leaver's roles.
API keys, webhooks, SSO and integration secrets are your settings; country packs and the API reference are maintained by PeopleOS.

M06.intro: Workflows automate how a request or event moves through people: approvals, tasks, conditions, notifications and record updates. Policies hold your organisation's rules (leave, attendance, expense and others) as dated versions assigned to groups of employees.
M06.why: A workflow decides who approves what and escalates when nobody acts; a policy decides what each employee is entitled to. A wrong route or a policy that is saved but not published silently changes what employees get.
M06.who: Tenant HR Admin holds workflow.* and policy.*. HR Manager can view workflows and start runs. Expense Admin can create, update and publish policies. Account Owner, Attendance Admin and Auditor can view policies; Auditor can view workflows and runs. Tenant Super Admin holds every key.
M06.where: Workflows › Process flows › Workflows and Runs; Workflows › Policies. Related settings in Admin › Setup › Automation.
objectives: Create a workflow, build its steps, check it and publish it, and follow its runs.
Explain the life of a request: raised, routed, decided, sent back, escalated, cancelled and audited.
Create and publish a policy, choose who it applies to and from when, and confirm it is really in force.
depends_on: M05 Users, access and integrations: approver roles, users and their access scope
M07 Employees and the employee profile: reporting managers decide manager approvals
M02 My work and approvals: where approvers act on workflow steps
M10, M11, M15: attendance, leave and expense requests that workflows can decide

workflows/workflows.purpose: Lists your organisation's workflows: what starts each one, what record it runs on, which version is live, whether a draft is open and how many runs it has had.
workflows/workflows.when: When you check which processes are automated, or add or change one.
elements: The event that starts it automatically, or Started manually.
The record type it is limited to, or Any.
The live version (for example v1, or Never) and whether a draft is being edited.
How many runs it has had.
Trigger event, Runs on and Status.
Opens the workflow with Versions & builder, Runs and History.
workflows/workflows.permission: workflow.view to see; workflow.create to add.
workflows/workflows.limits: The example organisation has one workflow, Probation confirmation: Started manually, Runs on Employee, v1 published, no runs yet.

workflows/workflows--create.purpose: Creates the workflow record: name, key, trigger, the record type it runs on, status, priority and optional start conditions. Its steps are built afterwards on the draft version.
workflows/workflows--create.when: When you automate a new process or a new approval route.
elements: Name, key, trigger, runs on, description, status and priority.
Optional employee conditions checked before an automatic start.
Check the details before creating; the creation is audited.
Leave without saving, or go to the next step.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: What people see in inboxes and runs, e.g. Leave approval.

fields.label: Key
fields.meaning: Stable reference filled from the name: lower-case letters, digits and _, starting with a letter. Fixed after creation.

fields.label: Trigger event
fields.meaning: The event that starts it, e.g. Leave requested; Started manually starts from a record.

fields.label: Runs on
fields.meaning: Limit to one record type (Employee, Attendance regularisation, Profile change…). Blank means Any.

fields.label: Description
fields.meaning: What the workflow is for.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Active workflows start; Inactive ones never start.

fields.label: Priority
fields.meaning: 1–999, default 100. Lower is tried first when only the first matching workflow starts.

fields.label: Start conditions
fields.meaning: Field, operator and value on the employee (department, grade, tenure…); all must match.

workflows/workflows--create.after: The workflow is saved with a draft v1 that holds only Start → End, and its edit page opens. Nothing runs until a version is published.
workflows/workflows--create.depends: Roles and users that will approve; reporting managers for manager approvals.
workflows/workflows--create.limits: The key cannot be changed later. Some request types are decided by the workflow only when Runs on is set to that type (attendance regularisation, letters).

workflows/workflows--edit.purpose: Changes the workflow's settings and, under Versions & builder, its steps. Publish the draft to make it live, start a manual run, and see its runs and change history.
workflows/workflows--edit.when: When you build or change a route, publish it, or start a manual run such as a probation confirmation.
elements: Each version with status, nodes and flow. Open builder edits a draft; Check validates a version.
Copies the latest version into a draft to change. Shown when no draft exists.
Validates the draft and makes it live; running runs keep the version they started with.
Starts the published workflow by hand, for an employee you choose.
This workflow's runs: subject, version, status, current node and outcome.
Secret that receivers of webhook steps use to verify calls; More holds Rotate signing secret and Delete.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: Display name of the workflow.

fields.label: Key
fields.meaning: Set at creation.

fields.label: Trigger event / Status / Priority
fields.meaning: As on creation; a change applies to runs that start afterwards.

fields.label: Runs on / Description
fields.meaning: As on creation; blank Runs on means Any.

fields.label: Reason for change
fields.meaning: Recorded in the audit trail alongside the before/after values.

fields.label: Node id / Type / Name
fields.meaning: Builder: a short key used by edges, the node type (Approval, Condition, Task…) and its name.

fields.label: Mode
fields.meaning: Approval: Single approver, One after another, All must approve, Majority decides.

fields.label: SLA (hours) / Task title
fields.meaning: Time to decide before it is overdue (default 48); the title approvers see.

fields.label: Approver type
fields.meaning: Line manager, Manager N levels up, role, user, initiator's manager, functional manager, HR business partner, context field.

fields.label: Fallback approver type
fields.meaning: Used when the approver above cannot be found.

fields.label: Escalation steps
fields.meaning: After hours, then: reminder, escalate to manager, escalate to role, or decide automatically (last step only).

fields.label: Edges (From / To / Label)
fields.meaning: Who goes where; label yes/no after a condition, approved/rejected after an approval.

workflows/workflows--edit.after: Saving the header applies at once. Publishing retires the previous version; new runs use the new version, running runs keep theirs.
workflows/workflows--edit.permission: workflow.update to edit and build; workflow.publish to publish; workflow.run to start a run; workflow.delete to delete.
workflows/workflows--edit.depends: A draft version to build; publishing needs a valid definition.
workflows/workflows--edit.limits: Only a draft can be edited; a published version is read-only. The builder is a form of nodes and edges, not a drawing canvas.

workflows/runs.purpose: Every workflow run in the organisation: which workflow, what it is about, its status, the node it is at and the outcome. Open one to see its tasks and its step-by-step log.
workflows/runs.when: When you follow a request through its route, find why it is stuck, or cancel a run.
elements: Running, Waiting, Sent back, Completed, Cancelled or Failed.
The node the run is at; the result when it ended (approved, rejected, completed, cancelled).
Workflow, version, subject, current node, who started it, dates and any Error.
Each task with assignee, status, decision, note, due date and escalation level, with Approve, Reject and Reassign.
Every action in order: started, task created, reminded, escalated, decided, completed.

steps: Go to Workflows › Process flows › Workflows and click New workflow.
Enter the Name; the Key fills in. Choose the Trigger event, for example Leave requested.

procedures.title: Example: build and publish a two-level leave approval
procedures.before: A workflow with Trigger event Leave requested and Runs on Any. Employees have reporting managers with sign-ins; someone active holds HR Manager.
steps: Open the workflow, tab Versions & builder, and click Open builder on the draft row.
Add node manager_approval: Type Approval, Mode Single approver, Approver type Line manager of the subject employee, SLA 48.
On the same node set Fallback approver type Anyone holding a role, Role HR Manager.
Add node long_leave: Type Condition, field days, operator greater than, value 3.
Add node hr_approval: Type Approval, Approver type Anyone holding a role, Role HR Manager.
start→manager_approval; manager_approval→long_leave [approved]; long_leave→hr_approval [yes]; long_leave→end [no]; hr_approval→end [approved]. Remove start→end.
Save, click Check on the draft, then Publish draft with a reason.
procedures.result: New leave requests of more than three days go to the manager, then HR; shorter ones only to the manager. A rejection at any step ends the run and rejects the leave.

procedures.title: Change a live workflow safely

Click Publish draft and give a reason.

procedures.result: New runs follow the new version. Runs already in progress finish on the version they started with.

Click Start a run and choose the Employee.
The run page opens: the manager has the task Recommend confirmation for the employee.
After the manager approves, anyone holding HR Manager gets Confirm <employee>. A rejection at either step ends the run.
Then the Update record step (Stamp confirmation date) runs and the employee and manager are told in-app and by e-mail.
Open the run: Status Completed and the Run log show each step. Check the employee's confirmation date on the profile.

warnings.title: Configuring a workflow is not processing a request
warnings.headline: Building and publishing a workflow sets the route; each request then runs through it on its own.
warnings.body: Configuration happens on Workflows (the definition and its versions). Processing happens in runs, tasks and inbox decisions. A change to the definition never changes runs already in progress.
points: Raised: the module records the request and fires its trigger.
Routed: every active, published workflow on that trigger whose Runs on and start conditions match starts a run.
Decided: approvers act in the Inbox; the outcome approves or rejects the request.
Without a deciding run, the request waits for holders of the approval right in scope.

warnings.title: Label the edges after an approval
warnings.headline: An unlabelled edge is followed whatever the decision, including a rejection.
warnings.body: After an Approval node, label the edge to the next step "approved". With no "rejected" edge, a rejection goes to End and the request is rejected.
points: Condition nodes need both a yes and a no edge.
Use Check before publishing; Publish refuses an invalid definition.
warnings.todo: Check every approval node's edges before you publish.

warnings.title: Cancelling a run does not cancel the request
warnings.headline: A cancelled or failed run lets the request go back to its direct approvers.
warnings.body: The request stays pending. For leave, for example, people with leave approval in scope can then decide it in the Inbox. A failed run cannot be restarted.
points: Reassign a waiting task rather than cancelling when the route is right.
Fix the cause of a failure before the next request arrives.

warnings.title: Which requests a workflow really decides
warnings.headline: Only some request types take their decision from a workflow's outcome.
warnings.body: Leave, time office requests, expense reports, travel, asset requests, loans, claims, variable pay, investment declarations, compensation changes, resignations and profile changes (including bank details) can be decided by a workflow.
points: Attendance regularisations and letters: only when Runs on is set to that type.
Transfers stay with people who can change positions; a workflow on Transfer requested only runs alongside.
Payroll runs are approved on the payroll run itself; Payroll finalized and Payroll paid only start follow-up workflows.

warnings.title: Never assume a policy is active because it is saved
warnings.headline: A policy applies only when it is Active, has a matching assignment rule and a published version in force on the date.
warnings.body: Save as draft puts nothing in force. A Publish from date in the future means today's rules still apply. Inactive, no rules or None published means the policy applies to nobody.
points: Saving the wizard stores the applicability rules at once, even for a draft.
Employees caught by a draft-only policy's rules get no policy of that type until it is published, if that rule comes first.
Among matching rules of a type, the lowest priority wins: named employees, then groups, then everyone.

warnings.body: A manager approval needs a current reporting manager with a sign-in. The step's fallback approver is tried next, then the manager reliever set in Admin › Setup › Automation.
points: A role nobody active holds goes to the role's reliever, if one is set.
An inactive manager with no reliever still receives the task: reassign it.
